title: Register and recover the command-usage journal
summary: Register an installed program inventory, inspect recorded observations, and safely back up or restore compatible private Chancery usage history.
use_when: Programs have been installed or updated and their command inventories require explicit registration.
The private command-usage journal needs scoped inspection, backup, or compatible restoration.
do_not_use_when: The caller needs token accounting, proof of product success, journal pruning, or migration of unsupported state.
outcome: Intended command identities are retained, recorded observations are inspected, or compatible private history is restored and verified.
effects: Registration can initialize only an empty supported journal and idempotently add identities.
Report dispatch can append its own metadata-only observation.
Authorized restoration selects compatible backed-up journal files after writers stop; the prior history is preserved.
authority: Chancery owns the journal and interpretation. Programs own instrumentation and product success.
File permissions form the current-user trust boundary; supplied threads do not authenticate callers.
success: Expected registered identities or restored history are confirmed through supported systems, command, and event reports.
Selected recorded counts are reported with gaps and database-local cursor scope preserved.
failure_and_recovery: Stop on unsupported or foreign state, invalid identity, unproven writer quiescence, or incompatible backup.
Repeat only unchanged idempotent registration after diagnosing its cause; do not retry uncertain recording or product work to obtain a usage row.
privacy: Keep the journal and backups private. Store no prompts, credentials, arguments, output, or domain outcomes in identities.
session_surfaces: current-user private journal and consistent backup tools
does_not_authorize: Executing product work, altering or pruning observations, bypassing triggers, or migrating unsupported state.
Retrying uncertain writes or treating absence as exhaustive usage proof.
steps: Select the intended private journal and preserve existing history.
Run each selected installed program registration mode or explicit registration interfaces.
Verify expected identities and selected recorded observations with supported reports.
Create a consistent private backup; stop all writers before restoring a compatible pair.
Verify restored history, re-establish database-local cursors, and resume writers.
checkpoints: The journal is empty or supported owned state before initialization.
Registration and instrumentation are interpreted separately from program installation.
Every writer is stopped and the backup is consistent and compatible before restore.
adaptation: Use the explicit absolute journal override for intended isolated state.
Register both Annals programs and refresh affected recorder integrations through their owning installation paths.
stop_when: Journal state is foreign or unsupported, or a required identity is invalid.
Backup consistency, writer quiescence, schema compatibility, or private ownership cannot be established.

consumers.statement: Current-user operators may register participating installed inventories, inspect observations, or back up and restore the journal.

preconditions.statement: The intended private journal is identified. Registration accepts only empty or supported owned state; restoration requires a consistent compatible backup and stopped writers.

inputs.statement: Installed program inventories or explicit stable system and command IDs; selected report filters and database-local cursors; a consistent private journal/schema backup for restore.

outputs.statement: Retained identities, selected count or event reports, or verified compatible restored history. Registration errors remain separate from binary selection.

data_semantics.statement: Registration is historical identity retention. Usage observes handler entry, not success. Zero means no selected recorded invocations and cannot prove non-use.

identity_and_units.statement: System and command identities are opaque 1–128 ASCII metadata. Observation IDs order one database history; times and range bounds are whole Unix seconds.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Reports select committed recorded observations at their read boundary, including zero-use registered commands. Disabled recording, failures, and uninstrumented boundaries remain uncovered. Restore changes cursor history.

access.statement: The operation uses the current-user private regular journal and installed registration interfaces. CHANCERY_USAGE_DB selects an absolute override; empty uses default.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Registration preserves earlier identities and observations, may partially commit, and can be repeated unchanged. Restore preserves prior history and verifies a compatible pair with stopped writers. Program rollback does not erase newer rows.

operational_limits.statement: There is no daemon, retry queue, pruning, update/delete, or migration command. Explicit request-scoped recording is unaffected by environment disable flags; no duplicate suppression is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Journal schema one is separate from program release and contract version. Products never migrate unsupported state. Rebuild recorder consumers and update owned wrappers, hooks, and brokers when recorder rules change.

reliances.statement: Journal administration uses local owned state; it invokes no Codex lookup or represented-product runtime work.
